p0_findings.mutable_exact_class_dictionary_alias: Both exact permit classes are exported as mutable Python class objects. Replacing __hash__ and __eq__ lets an object.__new__ instance compare equal to a legitimately minted dict key and pop its closure record, producing a typed receipt.
p0_findings.reflective_closure_registry_mutation: The production_minted and synthetic_minted dictionaries are retrievable through function.__closure__. A caller can insert an unminted exact object and caller-chosen record, after which consume() emits the corresponding typed provenance receipt.
p0_findings.production_impact: A PRODUCTION_REAL_DISK receipt was emitted from a reflectively inserted record with caller-selected free_bytes_before=1152921504606846976 without invoking the production issuer for that handle.
p0_findings.threat_model_consistency: M1576 already treats same-process object.__new__ reflection as adversarial. Under that same threat model, class and closure reflection cannot be excluded without an explicit boundary change.

verdict.minimal_successor: Do not export an in-process permit object as the authority. Move issue, disk check, consume, and producer construction into one clean fixed-entry child process so no capability object or registry crosses into caller-controlled Python. Alternatively narrow the threat model explicitly; an in-process Python closure cannot be claimed as a security boundary against reflective code.
verdict.ordinary_misuse_hardening_value: M1582 is materially stronger than M1574 against accidental duplication and the listed object/copy/exception cases, but that is insufficient for the adversarial provenance contract it claims.
